title: INCLUVIE FILM DISCOVERY
summary: Making representation meaningful at the moment of film discovery

children: Making representation meaningful at the moment of film discovery

children: Incluvie brought films, reviews, and representation signals together, but the experience did not clearly show how those pieces supported a viewing decision. The small team also held different views on what the homepage should prioritize. I reframed the site around the questions viewers ask while choosing a film, then used wireframes and prototypes to turn competing opinions into decisions the team could evaluate.

children: I structured the site around discovery, reviews, and representation cues; created wireframes and high-fidelity prototypes; and supported frontend implementation. The resulting system created a clearer path from curiosity to context while giving the team a shared reference for hierarchy and behavior.
The team left with a defined product story, a browsing path, and shared criteria for reviewing design decisions.
The decisions below show how representation became part of discovery rather than a separate layer of information.
Organized the site around the questions viewers ask while choosing a film rather than the existing page structure.
Used wireframes and prototypes to turn subjective feedback into specific decisions the team could evaluate.
Kept reviews, ratings, and representation cues close to each title so viewers could understand why it might matter.
Translated the direction into frontend-ready structure so the product logic carried into the built site.
A map of how viewers move from discovery to reviews, representation context, and a viewing decision.

children: The hardest part was not drawing the screens; it was making the decisions discussable. Clear wireframes and prototypes gave the team something specific to critique, which helped us align without flattening every opinion into compromise.
